isaac-sim:
Isaac Sim is a simulation platform for robotics development and synthetic data generation.
It simulates rigid-body dynamics, sensors, and photorealistic environments through NVIDIA Omniverse and PhysX.
It enables engineers to test autonomous behaviors and train models before hardware deployment.
It operates on workstation GPUs and cloud computing infrastructure.
nvidia-omniverse:
NVIDIA Omniverse is a computing platform for building 3D virtual worlds and digital twins.
It uses Universal Scene Description and real-time RTX ray tracing to synchronize multi-user 3D pipelines.
It allows developers to simulate complex physical environments with accurate materials and lighting.
It operates on RTX workstations, data center servers, and cloud instances.
newton:
Newton Physics is an open-source, GPU-accelerated physics engine for robotics simulation.
It evaluates multi-body dynamics, contact mechanics, and articulated systems using NVIDIA Warp and OpenUSD.
It delivers fast, differentiable simulation to train robot control policies and reinforcement learning agents.
It operates on NVIDIA workstation GPUs and high-performance computing clusters.
nvidia-jetson:
NVIDIA Jetson is a family of embedded system-on-module computers for autonomous machines.
It combines ARM CPU cores, NVIDIA GPU architectures, and hardware deep learning accelerators.
It delivers energy-efficient AI compute directly on robots and edge devices without cloud latency.
It operates as the onboard embedded computing unit inside mobile robots and drones.
jetpack:
JetPack SDK is a software development kit for the NVIDIA Jetson platform.
It packages Linux for Tegra, CUDA drivers, TensorRT runtimes, and computer vision libraries.
It provides an end-to-end software stack to build and deploy accelerated AI applications.
It operates on host development computers and installs directly onto Jetson target devices.
isaac-ros:
Isaac ROS is a collection of hardware-accelerated ROS 2 packages for autonomous robots.
It integrates CUDA, TensorRT, and NVIDIA Isaac Transport for ROS into standard ROS 2 nodes.
It lowers perception latency and increases sensor processing throughput for mobile robots.
It operates on NVIDIA Jetson edge computers and x86_64 workstation GPUs.
nvidia-halos:
NVIDIA Halos is a safety computing framework for autonomous mobile robots and industrial vehicles.
It combines onboard robot sensors with external infrastructure cameras to detect safety hazards.
It prevents collisions and improves operational safety in busy warehouses and shared workspaces.
It operates across Jetson edge devices, facility ceiling cameras, and central safety controllers.
nvidia-isaac:
NVIDIA Isaac is an umbrella platform for end-to-end robotics research and development.
It unites physics simulation, robot foundation models, and accelerated edge inference runtimes.
It streamlines the entire development cycle from synthetic data training to physical robot deployment.
It operates across cloud clusters, desktop simulation workstations, and edge robot platforms.
NVIDIA/tegra-nouveau-rootfs:
Tegra Nouveau Rootfs is a build tool that generates open-source Linux root filesystems.
It compiles the Nouveau DRM kernel driver and Mesa graphics stack for ARM processors.
It allows developers to run open-source graphics drivers instead of proprietary Tegra software.
It operates on host build workstations to generate images for Jetson TK1 and TX1 boards.
NVIDIA/cutlass:
CUTLASS is an open-source library of CUDA C++ template abstractions for linear algebra.
It decomposes matrix multiplication into modular hierarchy levels using custom tiling and Tensor Cores.
It enables developers to write custom, high-speed GEMM kernels without manual assembly coding.
It operates on host CUDA compilers and executes across NVIDIA GPU architectures.
NVIDIA/pix2pixHD:
pix2pixHD is a deep learning framework for high-resolution image-to-image translation.
It trains conditional generative adversarial networks using multiscale discriminators and feature loss.
It converts semantic segmentation label maps into photorealistic 2048x1024 synthetic images.
It operates on NVIDIA workstation and server GPUs running PyTorch.
NVIDIA/cuda-samples:
CUDA Samples is an official repository of reference implementations for the CUDA Toolkit.
It provides source code examples demonstrating memory management, kernel execution, and device synchronization.
It teaches developers how to write efficient parallel programs and utilize modern GPU capabilities.
It operates on development workstations running Linux or Windows with NVIDIA GPUs.
NVIDIA/DALI:
NVIDIA DALI is an accelerated data loading and preprocessing library for deep learning.
It executes image, video, and audio decoding and augmentation pipelines directly on GPUs.
It eliminates CPU bottlenecks and keeps training accelerators fully utilized with data.
It operates in deep learning training pipelines on workstations and GPU clusters.
NVIDIA/tensorrt-laboratory:
TensorRT Laboratory is a collection of C++ components for building inference applications.
It provides custom GPU memory allocators, thread pools, and asynchronous gRPC service wrappers.
It optimizes resource management and network throughput for high-concurrency model serving.
It operates on server-grade and workstation GPUs running Linux.
NVIDIA/video-sdk-samples:
Video SDK Samples is a collection of sample applications for the NVIDIA Video Codec SDK.
It demonstrates video decoding, encoding, and processing using dedicated NVDEC and NVENC hardware blocks.
It helps engineers integrate fast, low-latency video streaming into computer vision applications.
It operates on desktop, workstation, and datacenter NVIDIA GPUs.
NVIDIA/retinanet-examples:
RetinaNet Examples is a deep learning toolkit for single-stage object detection.
It trains focal loss detection networks and optimizes inference models with TensorRT and DALI.
It delivers real-time bounding box detection with high accuracy for robotics and surveillance.
It operates on NVIDIA workstation GPUs and embedded Jetson modules.
NVIDIA/jetson-gpio:
Jetson.GPIO is a Python library for controlling General Purpose Input / Output pins.
It provides a standard software API that interacts with Jetson onboard hardware registers.
It allows developers to interface external sensors, actuators, and LEDs with minimal code changes.
It operates on NVIDIA Jetson embedded developer boards such as Orin, Xavier, and Nano.
NVIDIA/jetson-rdma-picoevb:
Jetson RDMA PicoEVB is a hardware demonstration project for GPUDirect RDMA.
It enables an external PCIe FPGA device to read and write CUDA device memory directly.
It eliminates CPU host memory copy overhead for low-latency sensor data ingestion.
It operates on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Xavier boards connected to M.2 FPGA hardware.
NVIDIA/TensorRT:
NVIDIA TensorRT is an SDK for high-performance deep learning inference.
It optimizes neural networks through layer fusion, precision calibration, and kernel auto-tuning.
It maximizes inference throughput and minimizes latency for real-time robotic applications.
It operates across Jetson edge devices, RTX workstations, and cloud GPU instances.
NVIDIA/CUDALibrarySamples:
CUDA Library Samples is a repository of code examples for NVIDIA accelerated math libraries.
It demonstrates the use of cuBLAS, cuFFT, cuSPARSE, cuSOLVER, and NPP APIs in C++.
It guides engineers in accelerating signal processing, linear algebra, and image manipulation.
It operates on developer workstations and compute servers equipped with NVIDIA GPUs.
NVIDIA/object-detection-tensorrt-example:
Object Detection TensorRT Example is a Python application for real-time webcam object detection.
It converts a pre-trained SSD-Inception model into a TensorRT engine and runs CUDA inference.
It demonstrates how to achieve low-latency video inference and bounding box rendering.
It operates on NVIDIA workstation GPUs connected to USB camera streams.
NVIDIA/sampleQAT:
sampleQAT is a reference workflow for Quantization Aware Training and TensorRT deployment.
It trains a ResNet-50 network with simulated quantization, exports ONNX, and builds an INT8 engine.
It maintains model accuracy while exploiting faster INT8 tensor execution speeds.
It operates in PyTorch training pipelines and executes on NVIDIA GPUs.
NVIDIA/cccl:
CCCL is the CUDA Core Compute Libraries repository unifying Thrust, CUB, and libcudacxx.
It provides modern C++ parallel algorithms, device primitives, and standard library implementations.
It increases productivity by supplying reusable, high-performance building blocks for GPU programmers.
It operates inside CUDA C++ compilers on desktop, server, and embedded platforms.
NVIDIA/trt-samples-for-hackathon-cn:
trt-samples-for-hackathon-cn is an educational repository of TensorRT tutorial examples and guides.
It provides tutorials on custom plugin creation, model parsers, and inference optimization workflows.
It helps engineers learn practical techniques to accelerate deep learning models with TensorRT.
It operates on Linux and Windows workstations equipped with NVIDIA graphics cards.
NVIDIA/warp:
NVIDIA Warp is a Python framework for GPU-accelerated simulation, robotics, and machine learning.
It just-in-time compiles Python functions into differentiable CUDA kernel code.
It simplifies writing custom physics solvers, trajectory optimizers, and robotics algorithms in Python.
It operates on workstation GPUs, Isaac Sim extensions, and cloud compute nodes.
NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM:
TensorRT-LLM is an open-source library for optimizing large language model inference.
It implements FlashAttention kernels, KV cache paged memory, and in-flight batching runtimes.
It delivers high token generation throughput and reduced memory consumption on NVIDIA GPUs.
It operates on NVIDIA data center GPUs and RTX desktop workstations.
NVIDIA/nvImageCodec:
nvImageCodec is an open-source library of accelerated image codecs with a unified API.
It delegates image decoding and encoding tasks to GPU hardware engines like nvJPEG.
It accelerates image ingestion pipelines and eliminates CPU decompression bottlenecks.
It operates on Linux and Windows systems with NVIDIA GPUs and Jetson platforms.
NVIDIA/Stable-Diffusion-WebUI-TensorRT:
Stable-Diffusion-WebUI-TensorRT is an acceleration extension for the Automatic1111 Web UI.
It converts Stable Diffusion UNet and text encoder subgraphs into optimized TensorRT engines.
It increases image generation speed and reduces latency on local RTX hardware.
It operates on local desktop workstations and laptops equipped with NVIDIA RTX GPUs.
NVIDIA/ChatRTX:
ChatRTX is a reference application for local Retrieval-Augmented Generation chatbots.
It indexes local documents and photos using TensorRT-LLM, Mistral, Llama, and CLIP models.
It provides fast, private query answers directly from user files without cloud connectivity.
It operates locally on Windows PCs powered by NVIDIA RTX graphics cards.
NVIDIA/GenerativeAIExamples:
Generative AI Examples is a repository of reference workflows for generative AI applications.
It integrates NVIDIA NIM microservices, LangChain, and NeMo Guardrails into microservice architectures.
It accelerates the deployment of enterprise RAG systems, multimodal assistants, and agent pipelines.
It operates on cloud GPU clusters and enterprise Kubernetes infrastructure.
NVIDIA/nvmath-python:
nvmath-python is a Python interface for NVIDIA high-performance mathematics libraries.
It provides Pythonic bindings to cuBLAS, cuFFT, and cuSOLVER for CPU and GPU arrays.
It brings native GPU math acceleration to Python scientific computing without low-level C++ code.
It operates in Python environments on CUDA-enabled workstations and servers.
NVIDIA/Model-Optimizer:
NVIDIA Model Optimizer is a software library for deep learning model compression.
It applies quantization, pruning, distillation, and speculative decoding techniques to PyTorch models.
It reduces memory footprint and boosts inference speed for deployment in TensorRT and vLLM.
It operates during model preparation on Linux GPU workstations and cloud training clusters.
NVIDIA/TensorRT-Incubator:
TensorRT Incubator is a repository for experimental research and prototypes in TensorRT.
It contains community and research tools exploring novel model optimizations and compiler features.
It enables engineers to test experimental acceleration techniques before standard release.
It operates on development workstations running CUDA and TensorRT environments.
NVIDIA/Maya-ACE:
Maya-ACE is an Autodesk Maya plugin for audio-driven 3D facial animation.
It connects Maya character rigs to the NVIDIA Audio2Face-3D SDK and cloud ACE microservices.
It automatically generates facial motion from speech recordings to save manual animation effort.
It operates inside Autodesk Maya on Windows and Linux workstations with RTX GPUs.
NVIDIA/cosmos:
NVIDIA Cosmos is a platform of world foundation models for physical AI development.
It generates physical interaction videos and tokenized world dynamics using diffusion and autoregressive models.
It provides synthetic environment data to train robots and autonomous driving systems.
It operates on NVIDIA data center GPU clusters and DGX SuperPOD environments.
NVIDIA/Isaac-GR00T:
Isaac GR00T is a generalist foundation model for humanoid robots and physical AI.
It processes multimodal sensory inputs and language prompts to generate whole-body robot actions.
It enables robots to learn manipulation and locomotion skills across varied physical environments.
It operates on NVIDIA GPU servers during training and runs on Jetson Thor or Orin at the edge.
NVIDIA/TensorRT-RTX:
TensorRT-RTX is an AI inference SDK optimized for NVIDIA RTX graphic cards.
It accelerates neural networks using specialized Windows runtime optimizations and FP16 and INT8 kernels.
It delivers low-latency generative AI and vision model inference on personal client hardware.
It operates on Windows desktop PCs and laptops powered by NVIDIA RTX GPUs.
NVIDIA/GR00T-Dreams:
GR00T-Dreams is a synthetic trajectory generation blueprint for robot policy learning.
It prompts NVIDIA Cosmos world models with single images and instructions to generate robot interactions.
It solves robotics data scarcity by creating diverse visual training trajectories at scale.
It operates on NVIDIA cloud infrastructure and DGX compute clusters.
NVIDIA/3DObjectReconstruction:
3D Object Reconstruction is a computer vision pipeline that creates textured 3D meshes from photos.
It processes multi-view stereo images using Theseus pose optimization and neural surface reconstruction.
It produces digital 3D assets of physical objects for simulation and robotics tasks.
It operates on Linux workstations equipped with NVIDIA CUDA GPUs.
NVIDIA/Audio2Face-3D-SDK:
Audio2Face-3D SDK is a C++ and CUDA library for audio-driven facial animation.
It feeds speech audio into deep neural networks to calculate facial blendshapes and emotional expressions.
It automates realistic 3D character lip synchronization in real time without manual keyframing.
It operates on local desktop workstations and edge devices equipped with NVIDIA GPUs.
NVIDIA/OSMO:
OSMO is a workflow orchestration platform designed for scaling Physical AI development.
It schedules distributed jobs across training clusters, simulation environments, and edge hardware using YAML definitions.
It simplifies managing heterogeneous compute resources and streamlines complex robotics training pipelines.
It operates across Kubernetes clusters, cloud environments, and connected edge devices.
NVIDIA/TensorRT-Edge-LLM:
TensorRT-Edge-LLM is a lightweight C++ inference runtime for edge language and vision-language models.
It applies hardware-specific quantization and optimized attention mechanisms to small language models.
It provides fast on-device text and vision reasoning while conserving limited memory.
It operates on NVIDIA Jetson Orin and Thor embedded platforms.
NVIDIA/IsaacTeleop:
IsaacTeleop is a teleoperation framework for robot motion control and demonstration data collection.
It captures human operator movements using VR headsets or motion trackers and retargets them to robots.
It enables high-fidelity demonstration recording to train imitation learning policies.
It operates across Isaac Sim virtual environments and physical robot manipulators.
NVIDIA/ACCV-Lab:
ACCV-Lab is a software toolkit for training computer vision models in autonomous driving systems.
It provides standardized modular packages for sensor data augmentation, model training, and performance evaluation.
It improves model accuracy and streamlines end-to-end development of advanced driver assistance systems.
It operates on multi-GPU training workstations and cloud data centers.
NVIDIA/DreamDojo:
DreamDojo is an interactive robot world model trained on large-scale human videos.
It predicts future video frames and robot interactions based on action inputs and visual history.
It allows robots to practice and evaluate manipulation tasks within learned world dynamics.
It operates on GPU compute clusters during training and on edge workstations for planning.
NVIDIA/ncore:
NVIDIA NCore is a multi-sensor data platform for autonomous vehicles and robotics applications.
It defines structured component data formats and accelerates sensor processing using GPU pipelines.
It unifies camera, lidar, and radar data handling to improve perception throughput.
It operates on Linux workstations, data centers, and vehicle computing platforms.
NVIDIA/skills:
NVIDIA Agent Skills is a collection of tools for AI coding assistants.
It provides standardized skill definitions and CLI commands to interact with NVIDIA robotics and simulation software.
It allows autonomous coding agents to run Physical AI, CUDA, and robotics workflows directly.
It operates in local developer environments running coding assistants like Claude Code and Codex.
NVIDIA/elements:
NVIDIA Elements is a design system and UI harness for industrial AI and robotics applications.
It supplies framework-agnostic web components, design tokens, and command-line validation tools.
It creates consistent user interfaces for robot teleoperation, factory digital twins, and fleet dashboards.
It operates in web browsers and developer frontend toolchains.
NVIDIA/soma-retargeter:
SOMA Retargeter is a motion retargeting library for humanoid robots.
It solves GPU-accelerated inverse kinematics using Newton Physics and NVIDIA Warp to map human motions.
It converts human movement capture data into executable joint trajectories for humanoid locomotion.
It operates on CUDA-enabled workstations and Isaac Sim humanoid rigs.
NVIDIA/flashdreams:
FlashDreams is an inference and serving engine for interactive video and world models.
It uses custom CUDA kernels and memory management to execute autoregressive video generation loops.
It minimizes generation latency to enable real-time interactive simulation of physical environments.
It operates on high-performance NVIDIA GPU servers and cloud compute clusters.
NVIDIA/DeepStream:
NVIDIA DeepStream SDK is a streaming analytics framework for multi-sensor computer vision.
It combines GStreamer pipelines, TensorRT inference, and video hardware decoders on a single graph.
It processes dozens of high-resolution video streams concurrently with minimum end-to-end latency.
It operates on NVIDIA Jetson edge systems and server-grade workstation GPUs.
NVIDIA/halos-outside-in-safety:
NVIDIA Halos Outside-In Safety Blueprint is a reference architecture for facility-level robot safety.
It monitors robot work cells with external overhead cameras and calculates real-time hazard zones.
It expands the perceptual field of robots to prevent collisions beyond onboard sensor occlusions.
It operates on facility edge compute nodes connected to ceiling-mounted cameras and autonomous robots.
NVIDIA/NeMo-Speech.cpp:
NeMo-Speech.cpp is a lightweight C++ inference runtime for NVIDIA speech models.
It executes Nemotron speech recognition and synthesis models using ggml tensor computations.
It enables fast, local speech processing without heavy Python framework dependencies.
It operates on edge devices, desktop computers, and embedded CPU and GPU systems.
NVIDIA-ISAAC-ROS/isaac_ros_common:
Isaac ROS Common is a foundation package containing shared utilities for Isaac ROS repositories.
It provides Docker build environments, development scripts, launch tools, and automated test fixtures.
It standardizes workspace setup and ensures reproducible builds across ROS 2 nodes.
It operates on development workstations and Jetson targets running ROS 2.
NVIDIA-ISAAC-ROS/isaac_ros_dnn_inference:
Isaac ROS DNN Inference is a ROS 2 package for accelerated neural network inference.
It executes deep neural networks through NVIDIA Triton Inference Server and TensorRT engines.
It delivers high inference throughput and low latency for robotics perception pipelines.
It operates on NVIDIA Jetson edge modules and x86_64 systems with CUDA GPUs.
NVIDIA-ISAAC-ROS/isaac_ros_visual_slam:
Isaac ROS Visual SLAM is a ROS 2 package for real-time visual odometry and mapping.
It processes stereo camera frames and IMU measurements using GPU-accelerated cuVSLAM algorithms.
It estimates accurate 3D robot positions with minimal drift in GPS-denied environments.
It operates on NVIDIA Jetson edge computers aboard autonomous mobile robots.
NVIDIA-ISAAC-ROS/isaac_ros_argus_camera:
Isaac ROS Argus Camera is a ROS 2 sensor driver for CSI camera hardware.
It captures image buffers through the NVIDIA libArgus API and publishes standardized ROS image messages.
It maximizes video ingestion rates while lowering CPU usage through direct hardware access.
It operates directly on NVIDIA Jetson system-on-module platforms connected to CSI cameras.
NVIDIA-ISAAC-ROS/isaac_ros_apriltag:
Isaac ROS AprilTag is a ROS 2 package for fiducial marker detection.
It runs AprilTag localization algorithms on GPU cores using CUDA acceleration.
It provides fast marker tracking and precise 3D pose estimation for robot docking.
It operates on Jetson edge devices and x86_64 workstation GPUs in ROS 2 graphs.
NVIDIA-ISAAC-ROS/isaac_ros_image_pipelin:
Isaac ROS Image Pipeline is a collection of GPU-accelerated image preprocessing ROS 2 nodes.
It performs debayering, rectification, resizing, and color format conversions using CUDA kernels.
It offloads image preparation from the CPU to minimize processing latency before inference.
It operates on Jetson developer kits and workstation GPUs in camera processing pipelines.
NVIDIA-ISAAC-ROS/isaac_ros_pose_estimati:
Isaac ROS Pose Estimation is a ROS 2 package for 3D object pose determination.
It uses deep neural networks like FoundationPose and DOPE to estimate 6-DOF object transformations.
It enables robotic manipulators to grasp and inspect objects reliably in dynamic scenes.
It operates on NVIDIA Jetson edge controllers and GPU workstations controlling robot arms.
NVIDIA-ISAAC-ROS/isaac_ros_image_segment:
Isaac ROS Image Segmentation is a ROS 2 package for pixel-level semantic classification.
It runs deep segmentation networks using TensorRT to label each pixel in camera images.
It helps robots identify drivable paths, obstacles, and scene structures for safe navigation.
It operates on NVIDIA Jetson edge devices and GPU workstations in robot perception graphs.
NVIDIA-ISAAC-ROS/isaac_ros_nvblox:
Isaac ROS Nvblox is a ROS 2 package for real-time 3D reconstruction and costmap generation.
It builds truncated signed distance fields and ESDF voxels on GPU hardware using depth images.
It provides low-latency local 3D collision maps for the Nav2 navigation stack.
It operates on NVIDIA Jetson systems mounted on autonomous mobile robots.
NVIDIA-ISAAC-ROS/isaac_ros_object_detect:
Isaac ROS Object Detection is a ROS 2 package for image-space 2D bounding box detection.
It executes TensorRT-optimized detection models like DetectNet and YOLO over input camera frames.
It locates obstacles, pedestrians, and vehicles in real time with minimal latency.
It operates on NVIDIA Jetson modules and CUDA-enabled computer vision systems.
NVIDIA-ISAAC-ROS/isaac_ros_dnn_stereo_de:
Isaac ROS DNN Stereo Depth is a ROS 2 package for deep learning stereo disparity estimation.
It runs neural networks like ESS on stereo camera image pairs using TensorRT.
It generates accurate depth maps across untextured surfaces where classical stereo methods fail.
It operates on NVIDIA Jetson edge systems and robotics workstations.
NVIDIA-ISAAC-ROS/isaac_ros_depth_segment:
Isaac ROS Depth Segmentation is a ROS 2 package for distance-based obstacle detection.
It applies the Bi3D neural network to classify obstacles within configured depth planes.
It detects nearby hazards rapidly to trigger safety stops on mobile robots.
It operates on NVIDIA Jetson edge computers aboard industrial autonomous mobile robots.
NVIDIA-ISAAC-ROS/isaac_ros_nitros:
Isaac ROS NITROS is a hardware-accelerated ROS 2 message transport package.
It transfers image and tensor data between nodes in GPU device memory without host copies.
It drastically reduces message transmission latency and saves CPU memory bandwidth.
It operates within ROS 2 computation graphs on NVIDIA Jetson and desktop GPUs.
NVIDIA-ISAAC-ROS/isaac_ros_compression:
Isaac ROS Compression is a ROS 2 package for hardware-accelerated video encoding and decoding.
It compresses and decompresses H.264 streams using dedicated NVENC and NVDEC hardware engines.
It reduces network bandwidth requirements for remote robot monitoring without loading the CPU.
It operates on Jetson edge devices and x86_64 host computers.
NVIDIA-ISAAC-ROS/isaac_ros_cloud_control:
Isaac ROS Cloud Control is a ROS 2 node that implements the VDA5050 fleet protocol.
It translates MQTT mission commands from cloud fleet managers into local ROS 2 navigation goals.
It connects autonomous mobile robots to standardized industrial fleet management platforms.
It operates onboard mobile robots communicating with cloud or facility management servers.
NVIDIA-ISAAC-ROS/ros2_benchmark:
ros2_benchmark is an open-source benchmarking framework for ROS 2 computation graphs.
It injects test data, records processing timestamps, and calculates throughput and latency statistics.
It measures node performance under realistic workloads to find processing bottlenecks.
It operates on Linux development computers and robotic platforms running ROS 2.
NVIDIA-ISAAC-ROS/isaac_ros_benchmark:
Isaac ROS Benchmark is a suite of performance test configurations for Isaac ROS packages.
It uses the ros2_benchmark framework to measure frames per second and latency on NVIDIA hardware.
It validates that hardware-accelerated ROS 2 nodes meet real-time robotics deadlines.
It operates on NVIDIA Jetson developer kits and x86_64 GPU workstations.
NVIDIA-ISAAC-ROS/isaac_ros_freespace_seg:
Isaac ROS Freespace Segmentation is a ROS 2 package for navigable floor space detection.
It infers ground occupancy grids from camera images using TensorRT-accelerated segmentation networks.
It supplies navigable area boundaries to robot path planners to avoid collisions.
It operates on NVIDIA Jetson edge systems controlling autonomous mobile robots.
NVIDIA-ISAAC-ROS/isaac_ros_map_localizat:
Isaac ROS Map Localization is a ROS 2 package for global robot pose estimation.
It aligns live 2D lidar scans against occupancy grid maps using GPU-accelerated algorithms.
It resolves robot location within a pre-built warehouse map without cumulative drift.
It operates on NVIDIA Jetson computers aboard autonomous mobile robots.
NVIDIA-ISAAC-ROS/isaac_ros_nova:
Isaac ROS Nova is a software collection supporting the Isaac Nova Orin sensor architecture.
It configures and synchronizes wide-angle stereo cameras, fish-eye cameras, and 2D/3D lidars.
It provides complete 360-degree sensor fusion data for autonomous mobile robot navigation.
It operates on Nova Orin reference platforms and commercial autonomous mobile robots.
NVIDIA-ISAAC-ROS/nova_carter:
Nova Carter is a meta-repository containing ROS 2 packages for the Nova Carter robot.
It coordinates wheelbase motor control, Nav2 navigation, sensor drivers, and mission management nodes.
It serves as a reference autonomous mobile robot platform for factory and warehouse automation.
It operates on the physical Nova Carter robot powered by NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin.
NVIDIA-ISAAC-ROS/gxf:
Graph eXecution Framework (GXF) is a component-based runtime for hardware-accelerated compute graphs.
It connects modular C++ components and executes execution pipelines with low scheduling overhead.
It enables deterministic, high-throughput data processing across heterogeneous computing hardware.
It operates as the underlying execution engine in Isaac ROS, Holoscan, and DeepStream applications.
NVIDIA-ISAAC-ROS/isaac_ros_noetic_interf:
Isaac ROS Noetic Interfaces is a compatibility bridge repository for ROS 1 Noetic.
It generates ROS 1 message headers and definitions corresponding to Isaac ROS interfaces.
It allows existing ROS 1 systems to communicate with accelerated ROS 2 Isaac nodes.
It operates in mixed ROS 1 and ROS 2 robotics environments.
